cards.explanation: The answer is continuing in His word. Jesus says, "If you continue in My word, you are truly My disciples." Notice the word "continue," friends. He's talking about sticking with it, not just showing up once. A recipe only works if you keep following it, and I've learned that the hard way.

The answer is slaves. They say, "We have never been slaves to anyone." Now, friends, I'll just say it. Israel had a long history in Egypt, and God brought them out of it (Exodus 20:2). Jesus doesn't argue about that, though. He's headed somewhere deeper.
The answer is everyone who sins. Jesus says, "…everyone who sins is a slave to sin." Everyone, friends. No exceptions listed, no family-tree discount. That's the slavery the crowd hadn't noticed.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "A slave does not remain in the house forever, but a son remains forever." Two people live in that house, and only the son has a place there for good. Then Jesus says who can set people free.

The answer is Son. Jesus says, "So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed." Remember the picture of the son who remains in the house forever. Jesus is pointing to Himself. And "free indeed" means the real thing, not a sticker on the box saying free.

The answer is that His word has no place in them. Jesus says they are trying to kill Him "…because My word has no place within you." He doesn't say they lack a family or a name. His word just has no room in them.

The answer is False. Jesus says they're trying to kill Him, a man who told them the truth He heard from God, and then adds, "Abraham never did such a thing." So Abraham is the example they're not following. That's why Jesus says they'd do Abraham's works if they were his children.
The answer is God Himself. The crowd declares, "Our only Father is God Himself." Earlier they had said, "Abraham is our father…" Jesus answers that claim right away.

The answer is love. Jesus says, "If God were your Father, you would love Me, for I have come here from God." It's a test of the claim they just made. Jesus says that if God is their Father, they'd love the One He sent.

The answer is the devil. Jesus says, "You belong to your father, the devil…" He also says the devil was "…a murderer from the beginning…" and "…the father of lies." That fits the other father Jesus mentioned earlier.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "But because I speak the truth, you do not believe Me!" Sounds backwards, doesn't it, friends? Truth is exactly what they're not taking in. I think that makes it a pretty heavy moment.

The answer is that they do not belong to God. Jesus says, "Whoever belongs to God hears the words of God. The reason you do not hear is that you do not belong to God." He doesn't point to schooling or other teachers. It's about whose they are.

The answer is a Samaritan with a demon. The crowd asks, "Are we not right to say that You are a Samaritan and You have a demon?" Samaritan is the first thing they call Him, and the demon comes second. Jesus answers the demon part right away.
The answer is honors. Jesus says, "I do not have a demon, but I honor My Father, and you dishonor Me." Notice He answers the insult by pointing to His Father. That's where His focus stays.
The answer is True. They declare, "Now we know that You have a demon!" They'd already said it once, and this time they say they know it. Jesus's promise about never seeing death is what set them off.
The answer is greater. The crowd asks, "Are You greater than our father Abraham?" They point out that Abraham died, and so did the prophets. Then they ask, "Who do You claim to be?"
The answer is True. Jesus says, "If I said I did not know Him, I would be a liar like you." Then He adds, "But I do know Him, and I keep His word." He says it plainly.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see My day. He saw it and was glad." Abraham is the very man the crowd keeps pointing to. Jesus says he was glad about His day.

The answer is stones, friends. The verse says, "…they picked up stones to throw at Him." It's a heavy ending to the argument, and I think it's worth slowing down for. It comes right after Jesus says, "before Abraham was born, I am!"

The answer is that He was hidden and went out. The verse says, "…Jesus was hidden and went out of the temple area." John doesn't say how He was hidden, so I won't guess either. The text gives only that He was hidden and went out.
